title: Sparkline SDK faststart checklist & journal
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, action-first quickstart and ops scratchpad for the Sparkline SDK experiment. Goal: make an engineer (new to Redwood SDKs) go from 0 -> instrumented request in under 30 minutes and have a repeatable smoke + telemetry checklist for later handoffs.

Scope
- Covers JS + Python minimal installs, environment, example request, minimal telemetry events, and 5 critical smoke checks.
- Will be used by DX workshop facilitators and SEs for pilot customers.
- Not a replacement for full docs; this is intentionally terse and pragmatic.

Quick narrative
We repeatedly see new integrators struggle with three things: env auth (missing API key shape), network timeouts in corporate proxies, and silent failures when streaming is mis-wired. This doc surfaces those patterns and prescribes extremely small guardrails and quick tests to catch them early.

Faststart checklist (30-minute path)
1) Create API key (team-managed demo key) in Console -> copy to env.
   - ENV names: REDWOOD_API_KEY (preferred), RW_API_KEY (compat shim)
2) Install minimal SDK
   - Node: npm i @redwood/sparkline --save
   - Py: pip install redwood-sparkline
3) Minimal example (copy-paste)
   - JS: \n     const rw = require('@redwood/sparkline');\n     const c = new rw.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });\n     (async () => {\n       const r = await c.generate({ model: 'sparrow-mini', prompt: 'Say hi to team' });\n       console.log(r.text);\n     })();\n\n   - Py: \n     from redwood_sparkline import Client\n     c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])\n     print(c.generate(model='sparrow-mini', prompt='Say hi to team').text)\n\n4) Quick smoke checks (run in order)\n   - Auth check: set invalid key -> expect 401 with `invalid_api_key` in body\n   - Network check: run behind corp proxy (if available) -> expect 502/503 when blocked; add `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` test\n   - Streaming check: verify streaming endpoint returns at least one chunk within 1s for small prompts\n   - Latency baseline: 95th percentile < 800ms for the example prompt in hosted-us region (dev expectation)\n   - Token accounting: sample small prompt, check `usage.total_tokens` present in response

Telemetry & instrumentation (minimal set)
- Required telemetry events (names):
  - sdk.init (when client constructed)
  - sdk.request_started
  - sdk.request_finished (fields: model, region, duration_ms, success:boolean, fallback_used:boolean)
  - sdk.error (fields: error_code, http_status)
  - sdk.stream_chunk (only counts, not payload)
- Sampling policy: sample all init events, sample requests at 1% in prod by default; increase to 10% for pilot accounts.
- Local debug: set RW_SDK_DEBUG=1 to enable request/response verbose logging (sanitizes response text by default).

Minimal rollout plan for a customer pilot (15–30 seats)
- Day 0: onboard 1 integrator via this checklist in a shared Zoom session.
- Day 1–3: telemetry spike watch; escalate if sdk.error rate > 2% for 3+ hours.
- Canary: route 10% of requests to `sparrow-mini-latest` variant with fallback to `sparrow-mini-stable` on 5xx.
- Feedback loop: collect 20 sample completions and evaluate for hallucination/format regressions.

Failure modes & quick remediation recipes
- 401 / invalid_api_key: confirm env var name and key copy, check key permission (hosted vs dedicated).
- 429 rate limit: surface `Retry-After` header; advise exponential backoff with jitter.
- Chunked stream stalls: trigger a small non-streaming request and compare the two. If non-stream works, likely network/middlebox; suggest `fetch`/`node` TLS config tweaks.
- Silent success with empty text: verify model selection and prompt not empty; inspect `usage.total_tokens`.

Developer ergonomics notes (comfort items)
- Local emulator: provide `rw-sim` binary to mimic simple responses for offline iteration (TODO: improve fidelity for streaming).
- Snippets: make short interactive snippets for VS Code extension (copy to clipboard flow).
- Error copy: add small human-friendly messages for top 6 error codes in SDK (asked to DX writing).

Outstanding decisions / TODOs
- Decide default sampling rates for pilot vs GA. (PR open: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk#424)
- Finalize streaming backpressure API for JS SDK (proposal in PR: #431).
- Validate shape of `usage` object across JS/Py parity (owner: Priya).
- Add local `rw-sim --stream` to CI matrix (owner: Jonah).

References and quick links
- Confluence: DX/Sparkline-onramp-v1 (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub: sdk/sparkline faststart branch (linked above)
- Slack logs: #dx-onramp thread-482 has real-time notes from customer session 2025-02-25

Notes to self (scrappy)
- Keep this under one page. If workshop attendees ask for advanced topics: prepare a separate doc covering canary metrics dashboards, rollout SLOs, and cost/throughput knobs.
- For the workshop, bring a pre-seeded API key and a short rubric for scoring first-run success (3 checks: auth, sample request, streaming).

Session journal (quick)
2025-02-20: ran internal dry-run with SEs; streaming chunk delay observed in Windows WSL. Added note about TLS stack.
2025-02-25: pilot with Acme team — 5/6 devs got to sample request; one had 429 due to proxy caching (fix: bypass).
2025-03-05: merged small edits to env var docs and added README snippet for pip install.

End of doc.
